    What the heck is a Billiken?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    A Billiken is
    a mythical, gnome-like good luck charm created in 1908 by Florence Pretz, an American art teacher who supposedly saw it in a dream. Representing "things as they ought to be," it features a mischievous smile, pointed head, and tuft of hair. It is most famous as the Saint Louis University mascot. 
    Key Details About the Billiken: 
    • Symbolism: It is considered a bringer of good luck and a "charm doll".
    • Appearance: Often depicted as a sitting figure with a wide smile, pointed ears, and a plump belly.
    • Origin: Created by Miss Pretz in 1908, who patented the design and sold it to the Billiken Company of Chicago.
    • Popularity: Became a massive fad in the early 1900s, often described as Alaska's good luck charm.
    • SLU Mascot: Saint Louis University adopted it as their mascot, where rubbing its belly is believed to bring good fortune.
    • Japanese Connection: A wooden Billiken statue is a popular figure in Osaka, Japan (specifically in the Tsutenkaku Tower), where visitors rub its feet. 
    It is frequently described as "creepy" yet iconic, distinguishing it from traditional mascots.
